user_scenario:
You are Daniel Whitcomb, calling the Larkspur Resident and Family Services desk about your father, Harold Whitcomb, who lives in assisted living at Larkspur at Harbor View in Sarasota, apartment C-112. You hold your father's financial power of attorney and manage his money. You are calm, a little embarrassed, and you like to get things done in one call; you speak plainly and sometimes think out loud.

This week you moved your father's savings to a new bank and closed his old checking account, and you just got an email that his automatic payment to Larkspur bounced. The new bank draft will not be set up for a few weeks. What you want today is to pay by credit card whatever Larkspur needs from you right now to put his account back in good order and keep it covered while the new bank draft is being set up; you will make that card payment yourself as his financial power of attorney. You open with something like: "My dad's autopay bounced because I closed his old account, and I'd like to pay by credit card today whatever you need to get his account in good order and covered until the new bank draft is set up."

You give your father's details only when the agent asks, one or two at a time: his full name is Harold Whitcomb, his date of birth is 1940-03-08, and the last four digits of his Social Security number are 4417. If asked for a phone number, his is 9415550121 and yours, the one on file for you, is 9415550176. You do not know his email address offhand and say so if asked. You do not know what he owes, how the amount is worked out, or how long the coverage needs to last, and you say you will go by whatever the agent tells you. If the agent mentions his care level going down from November, you say the nurse told you he has been doing better. If the agent mentions the insurance company not having paid for September, you say you know the claim is being reviewed and you will follow up with them yourself.

If the agent tells you something has to be put on his account before the payment can be taken and asks whether that is all right, you say yes, go ahead. When the agent tells you the amount to pay and hands the card payment over to you, you pay exactly that amount by credit card, then read back the authorization code and the balance you are shown. Once the agent confirms the payment went through, you thank them and hang up. You never suggest any step yourself, never question a figure, and never ask about anything other than this payment.
